statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases within the low band after the index rejected the lower edge of the day's band, confirming two-way rotation rather than downside continuation.
recommendation: Conditions are described as orderly two-way rotation inside a narrow band with implied volatility decaying to a session low and yields retreating from their post-payrolls highs. A narrow danger window is flagged from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC covering the Friday power hour, the 20:00 UTC cash close and the 21:00 UTC Globex halt before a three-day U.S. weekend.
headline: Nasdaq-100 rejects its 29,450.37 session low and trades at 29,518.16 inside a 0.70 percent band, with VIX decaying to 14.03 and the 10-year easing to 4.770 percent from a 4.812 peak
body:
A third cash hour has been observed and it completed the picture the previous two suggested. The Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,539.57 against a 29,482.32 previous close, printed a 29,655.22 high, gave the entire advance back to a 29,450.37 low, and has since recovered to 29,518.16, up 0.12 percent on the day. Both edges of the day's roughly 205-point band have now been rejected. That is the opposite of the evidence class that precedes mean-reversion failure: retracements are arriving promptly and in both directions, and no extension has followed a failed pullback.

The macro trigger remains the August Employment Situation released at 12:30 UTC. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 55,000, the unemployment rate held at 4.1 percent, average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent on the month, and July was revised up to a 21,000 gain from a previously reported 23,000 decline. Interest-rate futures moved to roughly 59 percent odds of a quarter-point increase at the 15 to 16 September meeting, from about 55 percent before the release. The repricing is genuine, and four hours after the print its transmission remains orderly.

Cross-asset evidence has improved rather than deteriorated since the previous assessment. VIX traded at 14.03, down 2.03 percent from a 14.32 close and at the 13.80 lower edge of its session range, so implied volatility has continued to decay through the afternoon. The 10-year yield eased to 4.770 percent from a 4.812 percent session high and the 2-year to 4.364 percent from a 4.404 percent high, both retreating from their post-release extremes while remaining higher on the day. That combination, a front-end-led repricing that then stabilises, is characteristic of an orderly policy-path adjustment. West Texas Intermediate traded near 90.73 dollars, down about 0.62 percent, and gold fell 1.19 percent.

Index internals remain divergent rather than aligned. The Nasdaq-100 is modestly higher while the Dow is down about 0.48 percent and the S&P 500 down about 0.32 percent, and the Russell 2000 is marginally positive. Within the index, semiconductors have been broadly bid while the megacap cohort has lagged, and Tesla is down roughly 6 percent after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into the Cybercab. A single-name regulatory story and a semiconductor-versus-megacap rotation raise uncertainty, which is reflected in an elevated Stress reading, but internal divergence is the structural opposite of the aligned one-way path that would raise Tail. Tail therefore eases two points to 15 while Stress eases to 53.

The rest of the day is mechanical rather than macro. No further U.S. macro release is scheduled today. The U.S. cash close falls at 20:00 UTC and CME Globex equity futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend, so the final eighteen hours of the horizon carry no live price path at all. The narrow danger window from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC covers the Friday power hour and the closing auction, where position adjustment before a three-day weekend concentrates into a short span. U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are the Producer Price Index on 10 September and the Consumer Price Index on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.

The principal limitation is that this reading rests on three observed cash hours in a session whose remaining risk is concentrated at the close. A decisive break of the 29,450 to 29,655 band accompanied by shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements would invalidate it, and the danger window is therefore held across the late session rather than closed on the strength of an orderly afternoon.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours divide into three phases. Through the late 3 September U.S. session the assessment tracked a technology-led advance that held Tail in or near the watch band between 16:00 and 18:00 UTC as trend-up structure developed, with the Nasdaq-100 closing 1.16 percent higher at 29,482.32. Overnight the mode returned to normal and Tail fell to a trough of 12 as the advance consolidated without extension. From 04:00 UTC the scores drifted higher hour by hour as pre-payrolls positioning built, peaking at Tail 24 and Stress 76 in the 12:00 UTC slot immediately after the release, when the surprise was verified but no post-release price path was yet observable. The 13:00 to 15:00 UTC slots then eased to Tail 20, 18 and 17 as the release spike was given back, the cash open failed to produce continuation and the opening advance was fully retraced.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits cleanly at the weekend halt. Through the remaining cash session the modelled path holds in the low band on the condition that the 29,450 to 29,655 band continues to contain trade and no repeated extension after failed retracements appears, reaching its trough around 18:00 UTC when pre-holiday midday liquidity is thinnest. A lift into the watch band is modelled for the 19:00 and 20:00 UTC hours, where Friday power-hour flows, the cash close and gap risk before a three-day weekend concentrate position adjustment into a narrow span. From the 21:00 UTC CME Globex halt the final eighteen hours carry no live price path, so the modelled scores fall to a floor that reflects a closed market rather than an assessment of structure, then lift marginally as the accumulated weekend headline window grows toward the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen. Confidence decays steadily throughout because Friday's verified evidence ages without replacement. Beyond the horizon, U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.
